title: Hazel and the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1916, the army requisitions the coastal town of Brindle Point and its lighthouse, and keeper Cyrus Thackeray is ordered to surrender the parish ledger containing every name in town — including Elise Marchand, the French-born widow he secretly promised her dying husband he would protect. When a military tribunal declares resident enemy aliens must be interned, Cyrus falsifies the ledger to hide Elise and her daughter, gambling his post, his name, and his freedom. As the great storms of that year batter the coast and an investigating officer closes in, Cyrus must choose between duty to the crown and the promise made in peacetime; he ultimately confesses at the tribunal, loses the lighthouse, but secures Elise's release through testimony of her husband's service — and the three of them keep the light burning together as civilians until the century's wars pass.
about_author: Noor Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal municipal records from the First World War era. They write historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of paperwork and war.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Cyrus Thackeray's POV. A routine autumn night tending the Brindle Point light establishes his widower's solitude, his ledger-keeping habits, and his quiet friendship with the Marchand family next door. Emotional beat: grief held at bay by ritual and order.

chapters.title: A Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: two years earlier, Henri Marchand, dying, asks Cyrus to look after Elise and young Colette should anything happen. Cyrus agrees without understanding what it will cost. Emotional beat: the gravity of casual vows.

chapters.title: The Orders Come
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Grey lorries arrive; an officer named Captain Bell requisitions the town, the harbor, and the lighthouse, demanding all municipal records including the parish ledger of names. Emotional beat: the world reduced to what can be carried.

chapters.title: Names on Paper
chapters.summary: Elise Marchand's POV. She learns her name has been entered on the registry of enemy aliens and that internment orders are expected. She asks Cyrus nothing, but he sees the fear. Emotional beat: dignity under scrutiny.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV, night scene. Alone with the ledger before surrendering it, he weighs every name against his promise. He blots out Elise's entry and substitutes a dead woman's name. Emotional beat: first transgression, hands shaking.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Counts
chapters.summary: Captain Bell's POV. Meticulous and not unkind, Bell audits the requisitioned records and notices an ink inconsistency in the ledger. He files it away rather than raising it — for now. Emotional beat: menace in politeness.

chapters.title: Storm Season Opens
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus and Elise. The first great storm of the year batters the point; the light must be kept burning while soldiers fortify the headland. Cyrus and Elise work side by side through the night. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared labor.

chapters.title: Colette's Question
chapters.summary: Elise POV, largely through her daughter Colette, who asks why soldiers watch their house and whether Papa is coming back. Elise's answers reveal how much she suspects of Cyrus's risk. Emotional beat: motherhood as quiet courage.

chapters.title: Requisitioned
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. The army billets soldiers inside the lighthouse cottage itself; Cyrus is moved to a storeroom. His private papers, including Henri's letters, are nearly discovered. Emotional beat: home becoming occupied territory.

chapters.title: The Second Storm
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. A worse storm drives a damaged collier onto the rocks; the light fails mid-rescue when military generators cut out. Cyrus improvises, saving eleven men, earning grudging respect from the garrison. Emotional beat: competence as resistance.

chapters.title: Bell Comes to Tea
chapters.summary: Captain Bell POV. Bell visits Elise under pretense of a welfare check, probing gently. Colette innocently mentions 'Mr. Thackeray keeps us safe.' Bell begins assembling the truth. Emotional beat: kindness sharpened into threat.

chapters.title: The Smuggled Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. A letter arrives from Henri's old regimental chaplain confirming Henri's wartime service record exists but is misfiled. Cyrus realizes documented proof could save Elise — if he can get it before the tribunal. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Elise POV. Internment notices posted; neighbors she has known for fifteen years now avoid her eyes. She packs one small case, mirroring Cyrus's philosophy of measure. Emotional beat: the erosion of belonging.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Bell POV. Bell confronts Cyrus privately about the altered ledger, offering to lose the page if Cyrus cooperates in identifying other irregularities in town records. Cyrus refuses. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. With the third and greatest storm forecast and the tribunal set for Monday, Cyrus moves Elise and Colette to the lamp room to hide them from a surprise Saturday sweep. Emotional beat: love confessed in logistics, not words.

chapters.title: The Great Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The century's worst storm strikes; the light must be hand-turned when machinery floods. Elise works the mechanism beside Cyrus while Colette sleeps in the oil store, soldiers below unaware. Emotional beat: the promise kept in motion.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Bell POV. At dawn, Bell finds them — not by raid, but because he climbed the tower to help and saw everything. Instead of arresting them, he says the tribunal convenes in six hours and leaves the choice to Cyrus. Emotional beat: the antagonist's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: Tribunal
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Before the military board, Cyrus confesses the falsified ledger, presents the chaplain's evidence of Henri's service, and accepts full blame. Bell corroborates the service record and stays silent about the rest. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Elise POV. The board rules Elise exempt on grounds of her late husband's service but strips Cyrus of his post for falsifying official records. Elise speaks publicly in his defense, to no avail. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Relieving Keeper
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. A new keeper arrives; Cyrus packs what can be carried — Henri's letters, his father's barometer, little else. The garrison salutes him off the point, unprompted. Emotional beat: identity surviving the loss of title.

chapters.title: The Light Still Turns
chapters.summary: Elise POV. Spring: Elise and Colette have taken rooms in the village; Cyrus repairs clocks for a living. On clear nights the light sweeps over all of them equally. Cyrus and Elise finally speak plainly of the years ahead. Emotional beat: love after duty, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV, closing frame. Years later, Cyrus begins a new ledger — not of names owed to the state, but of debts of kindness: Bell's silence, the chaplain's letter, eleven sailors saved. He writes Elise's name first. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as what we carry forward.
